subject: Re: Request for operational proof of LLM no-training commitment
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@bridgewellhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bridgewellhealth.com>, legal@bridgewellhealth.com
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for operational proof of LLM no-training commitment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call this morning. Legal flagged a few items we need before we can sign the DPA addendum that excludes model updates from customer data:

- A current list of subprocessors and a snapshot showing which ones touch inference logs.
- A brief ops checklist or runbook that shows how you prevent tenant data from being used for model improvement (e.g., KV caching, training pipelines, retention windows).
- Confirmation on cross-border routing for Bridgewell customer data (we intend to keep processing in US regions only).

Can you send those as a single evidence pack for review? Samir (copied) is our technical reviewer and Alicia is legal. We need this by COB Friday to keep our onboarding timeline.

Thanks —
Alicia Ramos
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Bridgewell Health

[attachment: onboarding_template.docx]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@bridgewellhealth.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bridgewellhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for operational proof of LLM no-training commitment

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've pulled the checklist and current subprocessor snapshot together and attached three files: redwood_no_train_ops_checklist_v1.2.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_2025-11-18.csv, and export_controls_matrix.xlsx. High-level notes:

- Subprocessors: we include a CSV export with columns for role, region, data access scope, and whether inference logs are sanitized. Our serving runtime segregates tenant metadata from model telemetry and we mark "no-learn" customers in the routing layer so model improvement pipelines exclude their data.

- Ops checklist: covers request routing (policy tag: NO_TRAIN), KV prefix caching rules (eviction + per-tenant isolation), and the training-data ingestion gate (manual ACL plus automated label filter). It also calls out the QAT step that validates no-training customers prior to retrain windows.

- Cross-border: by default Bridgewell traffic (org id DW-4487) will be pinned to our us-west-2 and us-east-1 regions; we will not replicate inference logs to eu/apac locations without explicit written approval.

Quick answers to likely legal questions:
1) Do logs contain raw prompts? Some transient request logs contain prompt text for debugging but are ephemeral and retention is 0-3 days for no-train customers (see checklist page 3).
2) Can Bridgewell request export of all prompts/outputs? Yes — we provide SFTP export or API export; export_controls_matrix.xlsx lists formats and SLAs.
3) Subprocessor access: the CSV flags "inference-access" as yes/no; only a subset (monitoring and platform infra) have ephemeral access and are scoped by role-based policies and KMS-wrapped keys.

Marissa is looping in ops to own delivery and David will handle any technical attestation questions if you require a short call.

Next steps: please confirm whether you need an on-record attestation (signed) vs. an operational pack for your security review.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[attachments: redwood_no_train_ops_checklist_v1.2.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_2025-11-18.csv, export_controls_matrix.xlsx]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bridgewellhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@bridgewellhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for operational proof of LLM no-training commitment

Karthik / team,

Thanks for the fast turnaround — reviewed the CSV and checklist. A couple technical clarifications before legal signs off:

- The CSV lists a monitoring vendor (LoglineOps) as "inference-access: yes" and shows region=us-west-2. Can you confirm whether LoglineOps ever receives full prompt text, or only metadata/hashed indicators? If they do receive full prompts, what redaction/scrubbing is applied before access?

- The checklist references a manual gate in the training ingestion pipeline. Can you explain the controls around that gate: who can flip it, and is there an audit trail accessible to customers?

- On export: we prefer SFTP delivery to a Bridgewell-controlled bucket. Does your SFTP export include a manifest that maps session IDs to timestamps?

Also: we saw a line about retention 0-3 days "for no-train customers" — is that configurable per account? We need a guarantee in the contract language, not just an ops statement.

If it's easier, Marissa or David can do a short technical call today to walk through these.

Best,
Samir
Senior Engineering Manager, Bridgewell Health

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bridgewellhealth.com>, Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@bridgewellhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for operational proof of LLM no-training commitment

Hi Samir / Alicia —

Thanks for the review notes. Quick answers and actions:

- LoglineOps access: they receive only structured telemetry and hashed request indicators for monitoring. Full prompt text is never sent to LoglineOps. This is enforced via our log-forwarding filters and validated by an automated scrubber (see checklist sec 2.1). I've asked our platform team to produce a redaction sample; delivery ETA: EOD Thursday.

- Manual gate controls: the training ingestion gate is a privileged workflow in our internal "retrain" orchestration service. Only a small admin group in Research (RBAC role: retrain-admin) can approve a dataset for ingestion; approvals require two-person sign-off in the system and an immutable audit record (audit id included in manifest). We can provide a sanitized screenshot of the approval record for Bridgewell.

- SFTP export: yes, Bridgewell SFTP exports include a manifest.csv that maps session_id,timestamp,org_id,filename. We'll configure delivery to your Bridgewell-controlled bucket. SLA for exports is 24 hours for standard requests, 6 hours for expedited.

- Retention: for contractual language we can offer a retention cap of 72 hours for inference-text associated with a no-train designation, configurable to a lower value by request (min 24 hours). We'll ask Legal to propose wording for the DPA addendum that binds the 72-hour default and allows Bridgewell to request a shorter retention in writing.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Karthik / Legal to draft a short attestation statement (one page) confirming the no-training operational controls and retention commitment.
2) Platform to deliver redaction sample and a sanitized audit screenshot.
3) Bridgewell to confirm SFTP endpoint and desired retention SLA.

We can meet for a 30-minute tech+legal sync tomorrow if you'd like.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
